Final-Head Parity.given: The port is evaluated against upstream final head 7cf9e92c.
Final-Head Parity.then: The port contains proactive scheduling plus schedule/schedule_edit consent only; removed intermediate watcher, script_content, state-dir, gate-context, and connector-call features are absent, while ordinary pre-existing script/no-agent/monitor behavior is unchanged.

Final-Head Parity.given: LEO has conversation tools, direct operator commands, dashboard/API creation, and an automation-operator specialist.

Final-Head Parity.given: LEO's existing scheduler semantics are the baseline.
Final-Head Parity.then: Occurrence anchoring, bounded catch-up, deterministic idempotency, backlog deferral, one-shot retirement, manual-trigger isolation, terminal replay, and delivery receipts all remain unchanged.

Final-Head Parity.given: LEO approvals are durable, digest-bound, actor-bound, audited, and one-shot.

Final-Head Parity.given: An interactive CLI, TUI, static web/Electron, or answerable chat session has a bound notifier.
Final-Head Parity.then: Proactive guidance is present and a model create shows one schedule card before any row is saved; denial leaves zero rows.
Final-Head Parity.when: The model invokes a valid create.

Final-Head Parity.given: A model submits an invalid create.
Final-Head Parity.then: Bad schedule/timezone/workdir, no_agent without script, missing prompt/skills, paused_reason without paused, invalid wrapper/toolsets, invalid delivery/context refs, monitor conflicts, and unrecoverable past one-shots fail before any card and persist nothing.

Final-Head Parity.given: A valid create has omitted name, paused state, or a relative/absolute one-shot.
Final-Head Parity.then: The card uses the final saved/derived name; paused says it will not run and shows no first run; an active one-shot shows its absolute instant in the profile clock; a timezone pin does not falsely relabel or move that instant.
Final-Head Parity.when: Approval text is captured and compared with the persisted row.

Final-Head Parity.given: A valid recurring create has a schedule, zone, and run limit.
Final-Head Parity.then: The card shows normalized schedule wording, effective recurring zone, exact first run, and normalized N-run count; repeat supplied as string '3' persists and displays as three runs.
Final-Head Parity.when: The approved row is read back and compared with the card.

Final-Head Parity.given: The create uses prompt plus skills, script-only no_agent mode, an attached script, monitor, workdir, context_from, toolsets, or attach_to_session.
Final-Head Parity.then: The card shows canonical prompt and skills; no_agent shows only the script as the task; agent mode mentions an attached script; monitor script/URL, workdir, source IDs, explicit empty/nonempty toolsets, and session attachment are disclosed exactly as stored.

Final-Head Parity.given: A proposal contains a prompt or job body longer than the old preview cap.
Final-Head Parity.then: The complete proposal is transported and reviewable; no silent 300-character truncation occurs, and a surface that cannot prove full delivery offers Deny only.
Final-Head Parity.when: Long single-line and multi-line proposals are rendered.

Final-Head Parity.given: A create card is answerable.
Final-Head Parity.then: Choices are allow once, allow for this chat/session, always allow new jobs, and deny; once authorizes one canonical create, session/always affect creates only, and denial/timeout/cancellation persist nothing.
Final-Head Parity.when: Each decision is selected through every supported surface.

Final-Head Parity.given: The user denies, times out, cancels, or supplies /deny reason.
Final-Head Parity.then: The result is success=false with declined=true, saves nothing, preserves deny_reason/user_summary, tells the model not to retry, and does not count as a dangerous-command or tool-failure loop event.
Final-Head Parity.when: Four consecutive declines and reason-bearing denials are exercised.

Final-Head Parity.given: A model attempts to supply approve, first_run_at, approval id, or altered canonical arguments.
Final-Head Parity.then: Model input cannot forge approval or pin an unshown instant; consent is bound to the validated proposal, actor, resource, risk, expiry, and unique approval identity.
Final-Head Parity.when: Forged and replayed tool calls are dispatched.

Final-Head Parity.given: Two valid creates with distinct names wait concurrently, or persistence succeeds but scheduler registration fails.
Final-Head Parity.then: Concurrent valid creates have distinct proposal/card identities and transactional name reservation; one answer cannot resolve both.
Final-Head Parity.when: Parallel approvals and a registration failure are injected.

Final-Head Parity.given: A create card showed a future first run and the answer arrives before it.
Final-Head Parity.then: The exact shown first_run_at is saved for both one-shot and recurring creates, even if approval latency is substantial; the time is not recomputed from answer time.
Final-Head Parity.when: Answers arrive minutes later but still before the shown instant.

Final-Head Parity.given: A shown future first run passes while a create card waits.
Final-Head Parity.then: At or after the shown instant the result is declined=true, no row is saved, no approve-then-error occurs, and no different recurring occurrence is silently substituted.
Final-Head Parity.when: One-shot, every-2-minute, and every-minute creates are answered late.

Final-Head Parity.given: A one-shot is already due inside the existing grace window and no card is shown.
Final-Head Parity.then: The job saves with legacy grace behavior and no stale-card wording; the stale check applies only when a card was actually shown and its first run was initially in the future.
Final-Head Parity.when: A just-past one-shot is created in approvals-off/no-notifier context.

Final-Head Parity.given: An enabled job is updated with an equivalent recurring schedule such as every 24h versus every 1d.
Final-Head Parity.then: No card appears, the update is a successful no-op, and next_run_at is not re-anchored; a name-only update carrying the same schedule also preserves the cursor.
Final-Head Parity.when: Equivalent schedule spellings are resubmitted.

Final-Head Parity.given: A one-shot is moved by seconds or to another offset with the same wall-clock text.
Final-Head Parity.then: A schedule_edit card appears with the true instants, denial leaves the old instant unchanged, and approval stores the new exact instant.
Final-Head Parity.when: Second-level and offset-only one-shot edits are proposed.

Final-Head Parity.given: An edit changes a job to a one-shot whose new instant passes while its card waits.
Final-Head Parity.then: The edit returns declined=true before saving, the original job remains byte-identical, and no post-consent scheduler error occurs.
Final-Head Parity.when: The new one-shot instant is crossed during approval.

Final-Head Parity.given: A recurring edit is answered after its previously displayed first run.
Final-Head Parity.then: Normal recurring-update semantics apply and a future occurrence is computed from answer time; the one-shot-only late-edit decline is not incorrectly applied to recurring edits.
Final-Head Parity.when: A late recurring edit is approved.

Final-Head Parity.given: A model edit changes any behavior-affecting field.
Final-Head Parity.then: One schedule_edit card lists old -> new for prompt, no_agent, skills, context_from, semantic schedule, timezone, grace_minutes, catch_up, repeat, deliver, failure_deliver, attach_to_session, monitor, script, enabled_toolsets, workdir, and model/provider where applicable.
Final-Head Parity.when: Each field is changed independently and in combinations.

Final-Head Parity.given: An edit is invalid, semantically unchanged, name-only, wrapper-only, or has no listed-field change.
Final-Head Parity.then: Invalid edits fail before asking; equivalent schedule resends are no-ops without re-anchoring; cosmetic name/wrap_response-only changes remain unasked; no-card behavior is logged rather than misreported as stale.
Final-Head Parity.when: The invalid/no-op/cosmetic edit matrix is dispatched.

Final-Head Parity.given: A valid semantic edit card is answerable.
Final-Head Parity.then: Choices are Allow and Deny only; deny leaves the row byte-identical; allow applies exactly the shown merged update; no session/permanent grant is created; a cron_create grant never suppresses the edit card.
Final-Head Parity.when: Allow, deny, and prior-create-grant cases are exercised.

Final-Head Parity.given: The job is removed while an edit card waits.
Final-Head Parity.then: The save-time locked re-read returns a clear removed/nothing-saved error, does not crash formatting a missing job, and does not recreate the row.
Final-Head Parity.when: Deletion occurs during the approval wait.

Final-Head Parity.given: The job is paused or resumed while an edit card waits.
Final-Head Parity.then: The approved edit is refused as stale and the intervening enabled/paused state and schedule remain unchanged.
Final-Head Parity.when: Pause and resume are injected independently during the wait.

Final-Head Parity.given: Another surface changes any card-listed field or semantic schedule while the edit waits.
Final-Head Parity.then: The fingerprint mismatch rejects the stale save; the newer prompt, delivery, timezone, execution mode, or schedule is not overwritten.
Final-Head Parity.when: Concurrent edits are injected for every fingerprint component.

Final-Head Parity.given: A run completes while an edit card waits, or repeat is lowered below completed runs.
Final-Head Parity.then: Only the requested repeat limit is patched and merged under lock with current completed count; completed runs and next-run bookkeeping are preserved, and the card discloses N runs already done when lowering the limit.
Final-Head Parity.when: repeat.completed advances from 0 to 2 during the wait and the new limit is 5 or 2.

Final-Head Parity.given: An edit approval is waiting.
Final-Head Parity.then: No schedule write transaction is held during the human wait; the final existence/fingerprint check and write occur under the same jobs lock.
Final-Head Parity.when: A second writer attempts a schedule mutation during approval.

Final-Head Parity.given: deliver=origin and the captured origin exactly matches the resolved destination.
Final-Head Parity.then: The card says this chat only for the matching normalized platform/chat/topic identity and uses the scheduler's actual resolver output.
Final-Head Parity.when: Origin delivery is rendered for CLI, chat, and topic-capable sessions.

Final-Head Parity.given: Origin has no captured chat, or a configured home fallback exists or does not exist.
Final-Head Parity.then: The card names the real home channel or honest nowhere/history-only state and never claims this chat without an origin.
Final-Head Parity.when: Home configured, empty, and absent cases are rendered.

Final-Head Parity.given: Delivery uses explicit platform:chat[:thread], all, local, comma-combined tokens, a bare unconfigured platform, or a typo.
Final-Head Parity.then: Each token resolves independently to the explicit address, all home channels, local history only/nowhere, or an honest no-destination message; no nonexistent recipient is promised.
Final-Head Parity.when: The complete delivery-token matrix is rendered and compared with runtime routing.

Final-Head Parity.given: failure_deliver differs from deliver, or only the audience changes.
Final-Head Parity.then: Failure notices name their separate resolved audience; edit cards show raw token plus audience; jobs differing only by audience produce different consent text.
Final-Head Parity.when: Result and failure routes are varied independently.

Final-Head Parity.given: Command, schedule, and schedule_edit approvals use the shared card infrastructure.
Final-Head Parity.then: One frame/menu/dialog model renders schedule and edit bodies without synthetic command targets, Run wording, or dangerous-command labels; edit uses Change this job wording.
Final-Head Parity.when: All three known kinds and missing/unknown kind are rendered.

Final-Head Parity.given: An approval kind is absent or unknown.
Final-Head Parity.then: Rendering falls back to the existing command card and authority behavior; schedule wording never leaks into command approvals and command payloads remain compatible.
Final-Head Parity.when: Backward/forward-compatible payloads are rendered.

Final-Head Parity.given: Model-written text contains triple/longer backticks, links, spoilers, headings, HTML, or fake card lines.
Final-Head Parity.then: All proposal text remains literal inside one adaptive fence or escaped text node; no embedded markup can close the fence, hide text, or relabel the plan.
Final-Head Parity.when: Adversarial markup is rendered live, after timeout, and after a click.

Final-Head Parity.given: A native card send fails or the user invokes a plain-text approval path.
Final-Head Parity.then: Fallback and timeout text use the same dynamic fence and schedule/edit wording, state that no job/change was saved, and never say a command ran or waited.
Final-Head Parity.when: Native send failure, /approve text, and timeout rewrite are injected.

Final-Head Parity.given: A Telegram, Slack, or Teams schedule card is clicked, expires, or lacks a request id.
Final-Head Parity.then: Resolved and expired rebuilds retain schedule/schedule_edit header, body, choices, fence, and no-command wording; kind is carried on the prompt and adapter-local card state, not a duplicate global registry.
Final-Head Parity.when: Allow, Deny, expiry, and no-request-id paths are exercised.

Final-Head Parity.given: A classic/plain-input CLI panel cannot fit the full proposal.
Final-Head Parity.then: The complete body is printed to scrollback before the compact panel, no synthetic cronjob command is shown, edit choices are Allow/Deny only, and printed-above copy is emitted only when full text was actually printed.
Final-Head Parity.when: 100x18, 80x18, 100x14, 100x40, and long single-line cards are rendered.

Final-Head Parity.given: A TUI receives a long schedule or edit body.
Final-Head Parity.then: The body pages/scrolls through every wrapped line before a choice can be submitted, uses schedule/edit labels, and omits the synthetic command/view-command choice.
Final-Head Parity.when: Long command and long schedule bodies are paged with keyboard/event synchronization.

Final-Head Parity.given: A static web or Electron client receives or restores a schedule approval.
Final-Head Parity.then: The card is a turn-blocking approval with full proposal text and correct choices; missing folder/site target does not reject it; reconnect/reload restores kind and the same plan rather than a read-only generic blocker.
Final-Head Parity.when: Live, reload, restore-pending, and resolve-from-approvals-view flows run.

Final-Head Parity.given: A messaging adapter has a hard cap or Teams rich-text rendering.
Final-Head Parity.then: The full body is sent with a safe adaptive fence or the card is Deny-only; Teams shows literal text; no truncation can change the approved content.
Final-Head Parity.when: Caps, chunk failures, and triple-backtick bodies are injected.

Final-Head Parity.given: Existing command/folder/site/access/network approvals are exercised after the port.
Final-Head Parity.then: Their wording, targets, risk display, actions, and callback payloads remain unchanged except intentional safe fencing; schedule copy never leaks into them.
Final-Head Parity.when: Existing approval regression suites run.

Final-Head Parity.given: A schedule approval crosses canonical events, legacy server requests, or a gateway/managed worker frame.
Final-Head Parity.then: kind=schedule/schedule_edit survives every closed allowlist and transport; same-version workers validate it; missing/unknown kind remains command.
Final-Head Parity.when: Real frame serialization/deserialization and contract validation run.

Final-Head Parity.given: A client reconnects, resumes, restores pending approvals, or has multiple queued cards and answers a sibling.
Final-Head Parity.then: Replay preserves kind, choices, body, and request identity; answering one card cannot downgrade or resolve another; the restored schedule card blocks the correct turn.
Final-Head Parity.when: Reconnect, resume, queued-card, and sibling-answer scenarios run.

Final-Head Parity.given: A stale response arrives after timeout/expiry, or the same approval is tapped twice.
Final-Head Parity.then: The response is rejected without a second persistence or audit ambiguity; timeout remains a declined no-save outcome and cannot later authorize the job.
Final-Head Parity.when: Post-timeout and concurrent duplicate resolutions are injected.

Final-Head Parity.given: A user denies with a reason through legacy TUI/gateway paths.
Final-Head Parity.then: The typed reason reaches approval resolution and the model-visible schedule result; denial remains a normal user answer and leaves the store unchanged.
Final-Head Parity.when: Both legacy server-request and approval.respond paths are tested.

Final-Head Parity.given: The scheduling tool schema and system prompt are built.
Final-Head Parity.then: The schema stays neutral and teaches bounded one-shot/few-run use, self-contained fresh-session prompts, least useful cadence, update-existing preference, no retry after decline, and no autonomous send/buy/submit; imperative proactivity appears only in gated prompt guidance.
Final-Head Parity.when: Tool-description and prompt snapshots are inspected.

Final-Head Parity.given: The scheduling tool is direct, deferred behind tool search, or reachable through a tool-call bridge.
Final-Head Parity.then: Guidance appears only when the tool is actually reachable and answerable; reachability uses cached selection/check_fn results and never builds schemas, imports plugins, or reads forbidden files.
Final-Head Parity.when: Direct, deferred, bridge, unavailable-tool, and safe-mode prompt cases run.

Final-Head Parity.given: The port changes prompts, tool descriptions, contracts, locales, or docs.
Final-Head Parity.then: LEO's own token/count deltas are measured and reviewed, cron/unattended prompts stay unchanged, all artifacts are coherent, and upstream token counts are not claimed as LEO verification.
Final-Head Parity.when: Snapshot, generation, and documentation suites run.

LEO Adaptations.given: A live cron_create/session/permanent create grant exists.
LEO Adaptations.then: Future creates save without a card and proactive create guidance is withheld; every semantic edit still asks through cron_update/schedule_edit.

LEO Adaptations.when: Typed decisions and no-answer transports are exercised per adapter.

The corresponding LEO contract tests run.

LEO Adaptations.when: The corresponding LEO contract tests run.
LEO Adaptations.then: URL monitors use the existing public-address egress client and script monitors use the restricted runner; authenticated headers, private targets and browser rendering are rejected.

LEO Adaptations.when: The corresponding LEO contract tests run.
LEO Adaptations.then: bot-chat/profile map to durable local conversations; local:<id> and validated objects are native extensions; room requires a capable adapter and configured default channel.

LEO Adaptations.when: The corresponding LEO contract tests run.
LEO Adaptations.then: Every surviving field has a runtime consumer or an explicit rejection; unknown fields and removed intermediate scope never persist.

LEO Adaptations.when: The corresponding LEO contract tests run.
LEO Adaptations.then: Unknown, send-only, notifier-blind and ambiguous surfaces default incapable; only verified full-text, inbound-identity, terminal-rewrite surfaces receive cards.

LEO Adaptations.when: The corresponding LEO contract tests run.
LEO Adaptations.then: Existing @every schedules remain readable; any new @every compatibility is labeled LEO-native because final head rejects it.

LEO Hardening.given: A schedule was approved and later runs.
LEO Hardening.then: Creation consent never authorizes future sends, purchases, submissions, script execution, or plugin actions; each run uses normal runtime authority checks and the job prompt is self-contained for a fresh session.
LEO Hardening.when: Approved jobs attempt gated and ungated per-run actions.

LEO Hardening.given: LEO implementation and tests are ready for acceptance.
LEO Hardening.then: Relevant LEO suites run in an isolated clean environment with temporary home/DB, optional test dependencies installed, failures compared with unpatched main, and no upstream test result represented as LEO evidence.
LEO Hardening.when: The final LEO verification pass runs.

LEO Hardening.given: Credentials and clients permit live checks.
LEO Hardening.then: At least one live LEO gateway/model flow verifies create, deny, timeout, reconnect, callback authorization, rendering, and persistence; unsupported/unverified clients are recorded honestly rather than inferred from string tests.
LEO Hardening.when: Live smoke tests run after unit/integration acceptance.

LEO Hardening.given: An explicit destination is another thread/topic in the same chat as the origin.
LEO Hardening.then: The card compares normalized platform, chat_id, and thread/topic identity and shows the explicit destination, never this chat; both same-topic and cross-topic regressions pass.
LEO Hardening.when: Origin topic 10 is compared with explicit topic 20 and with a chat-only target that adopts topic 10.

LEO Hardening.given: A recurring create has repeat=1 or repeat omitted.
LEO Hardening.then: The card always states one run, N runs, or forever, and the wording matches stored semantics; paused cards retain the run-limit information without claiming a first run.
LEO Hardening.when: repeat=1, repeat>1, omitted recurring repeat, one-shot default, and paused cards are rendered.

LEO Hardening.given: A canonical API/Desktop approval response includes deny_reason.
LEO Hardening.then: The server accepts and validates an optional reason and forwards it to the model-visible result, or the UI/contract omits it consistently; no client sends a field the server rejects.
LEO Hardening.when: Canonical reason-bearing deny and reason-less deny are exercised.

LEO Hardening.given: An edit is saved without a card and the job changes concurrently.
LEO Hardening.then: The real shown boolean controls staleness; no-card model edits fail closed to approval_required, while trusted operator edits re-read and CAS under the write transaction.
LEO Hardening.when: Approvals-off/no-notifier edits race with pause or another edit.

LEO Hardening.given: A model tries to create/edit proactive work where no human can answer.
LEO Hardening.then: LEO explicitly chooses and documents fail-closed or durable proposal queueing rather than silent save; the choice is enforced mechanically, audited, and tested separately from final-head compatibility mode.
LEO Hardening.when: No-card policy is enabled across every unattended context.

LEO Hardening.given: An API client genuinely renders and answers approvals.
LEO Hardening.then: A per-request/client capability allows that client to opt into answerable schedule cards, while stock or incapable clients remain no-card; platform name alone is not the discriminator.
LEO Hardening.when: Capable and incapable API clients submit identical creates.

LEO Hardening.given: Concurrent creates use the same name/key, or a client retries after a lost response.
LEO Hardening.then: Same-key/same-args returns the original job/card state without re-anchor or duplicate card; same-key/different-args conflicts; same-name model create cannot silently overwrite/re-enable; lock degradation fails closed.
LEO Hardening.when: Concurrent same-name and same-idempotency-key creates are injected.

LEO Hardening.given: A naive ISO one-shot is supplied with an IANA job zone, or a paused recurring job has a non-profile zone.
LEO Hardening.then: Naive input either honors the job zone or is rejected before asking with offset guidance; aware input remains absolute; paused recurring cards still show the effective zone; DST and cross-zone cases are covered.
LEO Hardening.when: Sydney profile + Lisbon zone, offset-bearing ISO, DST transitions, and paused Tokyo-zone jobs are tested.

LEO Hardening.given: The shown first run occurs before the configured approval timeout.
LEO Hardening.then: The displayed deadline equals min(approval timeout, shown first run), or the earlier cutoff is explicitly documented; every locale derives the same effective window.
LEO Hardening.when: One-minute, every-minute, and normal-timeout cards are rendered.

LEO Hardening.given: The process restarts or adapter-local preview state is evicted while a card is pending.
LEO Hardening.then: Kind and full proposal survive in the durable approval row/event, so resolved/expired/restarted cards retain schedule wording on every adapter and typed path.
LEO Hardening.when: Restart, cache eviction, Feishu/Matrix/WhatsApp Cloud/Relay/typed-confirmation, and Teams-restart paths run.

LEO Hardening.given: A terminal shrinks while a card is open or a keyboard key repeats over queued cards.
LEO Hardening.then: Printed-above claims remain true after resize or are withdrawn/reprinted; held Enter cannot approve a schedule/edit card before it is visibly presented.
LEO Hardening.when: 100x40 shrinks to 100x18 and key-repeat queued-card tests run.

LEO Hardening.given: New workers/gateways deploy while old versions still run.
LEO Hardening.then: Version negotiation/draining/restart prevents closed-frame rejection or kind loss; old-version failure is detected and handled rather than silently degrading to command.
LEO Hardening.when: Same-version and mixed-version frame tests run.

LEO Hardening.given: Delivery resolution raises, or a capped adapter cannot send a full body containing triple backticks.
LEO Hardening.then: A preview failure does not break an otherwise valid no-card create; capped surfaces use the shared adaptive fence to send full text where possible instead of unnecessarily becoming Deny-only.
LEO Hardening.when: Resolver exceptions and fenced long-body sends are injected.

LEO Hardening.when: Remove/create replacement and resume are attempted under a create grant.

LEO Hardening.when: Mid-session policy and notifier changes are tested.

LEO Hardening.given: The user selects always allow new jobs.

LEO Hardening.when: Negative evals run with real tool dispatch and store assertions.

LEO Hardening.given: A date or scheduling instruction appears only in email, web content, attachment, or tool output.
LEO Hardening.then: Untrusted content cannot initiate a schedule card or save under a grant; only trusted user intent or an explicitly approved event-source policy may trigger proactive scheduling.
LEO Hardening.when: Email/web/tool-output dates and instructions are injected.

LEO Hardening.given: Active, paused, denied, dismissed, removed, or plugin-owned jobs already cover the same subject.
LEO Hardening.then: A list-first lookup and canonical when/what/who fingerprint prevent duplicate cards/jobs; near-matches offer update; denial/removal suppression survives job deletion; mentioning a paused job does not resume or replace it.
LEO Hardening.when: Seeded active/paused/denied/dismissed/deleted/plugin-owned states are proposed again.

LEO Hardening.given: A create is denied, invalid, timed out, or succeeds, and a monitored fact may become stale before delivery.
LEO Hardening.then: The one-line scheduled confirmation is generated from persisted tool state, never model prose; pre-delivery freshness/done-condition checks suppress resolved or stale alerts and distinguish false from read failure.
LEO Hardening.when: Failed/declined creates and stale/resolved/source-failure deliveries are exercised.

LEO Hardening.given: A scheduled run is silent, fails, completes without delivery, or a source is unavailable.
LEO Hardening.then: Every occurrence has a runner-authored receipt; missing receipt means not run; unchanged silence differs from failure; rejected/partial delivery is visible and sticky in continuity; source unavailable differs from checked-empty.
LEO Hardening.when: Silent success, crash, rejected Telegram HTML, partial delivery, and source outage cases run.

LEO Hardening.given: A scheduled job calls a plugin or outbound action that needs human authority.
LEO Hardening.then: Creation consent is not reused as action consent; the per-call gate resolves by explicit unattended policy and produces a durable actionable needs-you notice rather than silent default-deny or model prose.
LEO Hardening.when: Plugin approve/deny and outbound send/buy/submit attempts occur inside a scheduled run.

LEO Hardening.given: automation.max_repeat_runs is configured.
LEO Hardening.when: A model creates a recurring schedule.
LEO Hardening.then: The cap applies only to model-created schedules, is disclosed on the card, and omitted repeat remains forever when no cap is configured.

LEO Hardening.given: automation.proactive_mode is off or offer.
LEO Hardening.when: A turn evaluates scheduling guidance.
LEO Hardening.then: Off disables guidance only; offer uses the normal card path; neither mode bypasses consent or create grants.

Deferred.given: Approval mode is off or yolo is active, even if interactive flags are set.
Deferred.then: No proactive line and no card appear; the valid create saves as before, and an INFO log names approvals-off/yolo as the reason.
Deferred.when: A model create or edit is dispatched.
Deferred.disposition: removed from the core gate or explicitly deferred by the revised plan

Deferred.given: The context has no UI, is a finite/-q turn, or is a resumed session now running finitely.
Deferred.then: No card is created or awaited, explicit valid requests retain save-as-before behavior, and no static guidance promises a card where none can be shown.
Deferred.when: The answerability predicate and live gate evaluate the turn.
Deferred.disposition: removed from the core gate or explicitly deferred by the revised plan

Deferred.given: The turn originates from cron/scheduler, kanban/one-shot worker, batch runner, or a side/background agent.
Deferred.then: Proactive guidance is absent; no schedule card is shown; any explicitly requested valid create/edit follows the logged no-card compatibility path without parking an invisible approval.
Deferred.when: Each unattended worker context is simulated through the real registry.
Deferred.disposition: removed from the core gate or explicitly deferred by the revised plan

Deferred.given: An API/webhook turn is unattended, notifier-blind, or ask-mode chat has no bound notifier.
Deferred.then: No card or proactive line appears; the requested valid operation saves as before and logs the real no-answer reason, with no false decline or pending row.
Deferred.when: The live gate checks notifier/client capability.
Deferred.disposition: removed from the core gate or explicitly deferred by the revised plan

Deferred.given: A prompt was cached before a grant/mode/notifier change.
Deferred.then: The live gate still evaluates current approval state immediately before persistence; cached guidance is never treated as authorization and a present user's live no still prevents save.
Deferred.when: Mid-session grant/yolo/off changes and interactive-to-finite resume are exercised.
Deferred.disposition: removed from the core gate or explicitly deferred by the revised plan

Deferred.given: The model sees eligible proactive guidance.
Deferred.then: For dentist, flight check-in/airport/arrival, Lisbon arrival, owed Slack reply, deadline, water habit, and site re-check scenarios, the model invokes the tool rather than merely offering, proposes bounded useful cadence, and the card/store reflect the intended job.
Deferred.when: Held-out positive evals run through real LEO tool dispatch with store assertions.
Deferred.disposition: removed from the core gate or explicitly deferred by the revised plan

Deferred.given: Proactive scheduling is considered for default enablement.
Deferred.then: Per-model, held-out, multi-turn evals run with fresh homes, real dispatch, n>=3, provider-timeout accounting, small/local and frontier models, raw JSONL, latency/tool-cost measurement, and no aggregate-only reliability claim.
Deferred.disposition: removed from the core gate or explicitly deferred by the revised plan

Deferred.given: The user wants to stop proactive suggestions without disabling explicit scheduling or weakening approval protection.
Deferred.then: Independent create|offer|off controls, quiet hours, urgent override, interruption budget, and bounded snooze are deterministic; off stops proposals but not explicit jobs or already approved runs; snooze moves one notification, not recurrence.
Deferred.when: Config/card precedence, overnight deferral, urgent override, and snooze tests run.
Deferred.disposition: removed from the core gate or explicitly deferred by the revised plan

Deferred.given: A recurring job or one user moment could create several jobs/cards.
Deferred.then: Cards show resolved model and enforced run/token/cost ceilings; over-cap work is refused before wake; jobs-per-helpful-run and multi-card rate are measured, with grouping or one-job-per-moment behavior available.
Deferred.when: Budget exhaustion, cheap-tier routing, and multi-card scenarios run.
Deferred.disposition: removed from the core gate or explicitly deferred by the revised plan

Deferred.then: Quiet hours, urgent override, snooze, presence routing, calendar deferral, interruption budgets and deliver-where-you-are routing.
Combined multi-job cards, daily batching, per-kind trust ladders, broad dismissal learning and plugin tracked-subject hooks.
Event-triggered job cards, kanban wake-ups, commitment lifecycle, done conditions, freshness/source-health lifecycle and condition-based snooze.
Reply-to-delivered-reminder cancellation and a full public Inbox UI; only minimal authenticated operator proposal recovery ships.
Off-host scheduler heartbeat, tamper-evident receipts, output digest/schema verification, dispatch-acceptance scoring and native mobile controls.
Token or cost ceilings beyond the optional repeat cap, external-memory retention controls and hardened silent-marker parsing.
Public proposal list/resolve/dismiss APIs beyond the minimum needed to make approval_required meaningful; the dashboard/TUI operator recovery path is the v1 surface.
Native approval controls for all 22 LEO adapters; TUI, web/Electron stream and Telegram are the initial card surfaces, and all others remain incapable.
The multi-model held-out evaluation campaign as a release gate; it gates autonomous create mode only, not the consent plumbing.
Semantic near-match subject dedupe; exact canonical dedupe, duplicate-name conflict and request idempotency ship instead.
Locale-catalog parity and prompt-cache invalidation; both are not applicable to LEO as architected and are replaced by contract tests.
External scheduler-registration hooks and scheduler_registered result fields; LEO's durable schedule row is already the scheduler input.
A separate schedule_occurrences receipt store or UI; existing task metadata task.delivery remains authoritative.
Additional Bot Chat/Room connectors beyond durable local conversations and room-capable adapters; unsupported room tokens are rejected at validation.
Reply-to-delivered-reminder conversation continuation beyond the attach_to_session brief; full two-way job chat is future scope.

Deferred.given: A durable schedule row is the scheduler input.
Deferred.then: No scheduler_registered result field or external registration hook is shipped; LEO's durable row is already the scheduler input.
Read-only export comparison is follow-up scope; native monitor baseline/change/failure semantics remain in the core gate.
